test_title: PYST 29: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following specific subgroup receives treatment for diarrhoea under the Stop Diarrhoea Campaign launched in June/July 2025?

options.text: Children under five suffering from diarrhoea
Rural children above six years with diarrhoea

solution:
The correct answer is __**Children under five suffering from diarrhoea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Stop Diarrhoea Campaign** was strategically launched to address the critical issue of child mortality, specifically targeting **children under five years of age**. This demographic is most vulnerable to the dehydrating effects of diarrhoeal diseases.
 
• In **June/July 2024** (with cycles continuing into **2025**), the **Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** rebranded the existing **Intensified Diarrhoea Control Fortnight (IDCF)** into a more comprehensive **two-month-long campaign**.
 
• The primary objective of the campaign is **"Zero Childhood Diarrhoea Deaths,"** emphasizing that no child should lose their life to a preventable and treatable condition like diarrhoea.
 
• The campaign involves the distribution of **ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)** and **Zinc tablets** to families with **children under five**. While **ORS** helps in immediate rehydration, **Zinc** reduces the duration and severity of the episode. ***Hence, the specific subgroup receiving treatment is children under five.***
 
• The **Union Health Minister**, **Shri J.P. Nadda**, highlighted the shift from a **14-day** strategy to a **60-day** intensive program to ensure wider reach and better health outcomes across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diarrhoea and Child Mortality:** Diarrhoea remains a leading cause of death among **children under five** globally and in **India**. It results in severe dehydration and loss of essential minerals, which can be fatal if not managed timely with **rehydration therapy**.
 
• **Role of Frontline Workers:** **ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist)** workers play a pivotal role in this campaign by conducting **house-to-house visits** to distribute **ORS** packets and educate mothers about **infant and young child feeding (IYCF)** practices.
 
• **ORS and Zinc Combination:** The **World Health Organization (WHO)** recommends the use of **low-osmolarity ORS** and **Zinc supplementation** for **14 days** as the gold standard for treating childhood diarrhoea. **Zinc** not only treats the current episode but also prevents future episodes for the next **2 to 3 months**.
 
• **NFHS-5 Data:** According to the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5)**, while there has been an improvement in the usage of **ORS**, awareness regarding the importance of **Zinc** therapy still needs significant enhancement among rural and urban populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **WASH Initiatives:** The campaign is closely linked with **WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene)** goals. It encourages **handwashing with soap**, the use of **safe drinking water**, and the **hygienic disposal of waste** to prevent the spread of enteric pathogens.
 
• **Vaccination:** Besides treatment, the **Government of India** provides the **Rotavirus vaccine** under the **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)**, which significantly reduces the incidence of severe diarrhoea caused by **Rotavirus** in infants.
 
• **Public Awareness:** The **Stop Diarrhoea Campaign 2025** utilizes **mass media**, **digital platforms**, and **community meetings** to spread the message of "**Sahi Poshan, Desh Roshan**" (Right Nutrition, Bright Nation), ensuring parents understand the importance of **continued breastfeeding** during illness.
 
• **Monitoring:** **District and State-level** health officials are tasked with monitoring the distribution chain to ensure that there is no shortage of **ORS** and **Zinc** during the **monsoon season**, which typically sees a spike in water-borne diseases.
